Senses.Explanation: Yi!: a written vocal interjection that punctuates a turn, often pivoting from a question or exposition into a capping line. Rujing, Pu'an, Wuming, Tianyin, Poshan, Yongjue, and Zhuanyu place the cry at a rhetorical hinge: after a question, reversal, or exposition and immediately before a compact capping response.
Senses.Note: Its force depends on voice and position. English punctuation or interjections may vary by scene; retaining “Yi!” preserves the audible marker without assigning one emotion everywhere.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the work of liberating people was already complete
AlternateTargets: the work of delivering people was already complete
SearchAliases: before leaving the womb the work was complete
Senses.Explanation: The records use 度人已畢 to reverse ordinary sequence: the work of liberating people is already complete before birth or another apparent beginning. It most often forms the second half of 未出母胎，度人已畢: before leaving the womb, the work was done. Zhongfeng Mingben and Foyan Qingyuan use the inherited line to put activity before the narrated birth; Miyun Yuanwu applies its two halves to dependence on parents and teachers; Wunian You pairs it with teaching already complete before the mouth opens; Feiyin Tongrong treats it as an inability to conceal what is already present; and an unnamed monk questioning Poshan Haiming independently reapplies the shorter predicate to thirty-six years of a teacher's life.
Senses.Note: 度人 literally concerns bringing or carrying people across and conventionally means delivering or liberating them. Preserve the completed-action force of 已畢. The phrase does not mean that a later teaching career historically ended before birth; the retained masters use and test the inherited formula as a temporal reversal.
